svg.title: The RAG quality quartet as a two-by-two
svg.desc: A two-by-two grid of the four RAG evaluation signals, split into a retriever side and a generator side. The left blue column is the retriever, answering "did we fetch the right context?" and holds two cards: Context precision, defined as relevant retrieved divided by total retrieved (did we pull junk alongside the good page?), and Context recall, defined as relevant retrieved divided by total relevant (did we miss a needed page?). The right green column is the generator, answering "did we use the context well?" and holds two cards: Faithfulness, meaning every claim is supported by the retrieved context with nothing invented, and Answer relevance, meaning the answer actually addresses the question and is not evasive or off topic. A footer band explains that whichever quadrant drops localizes the fix: context recall of zero points to fixing retrieval, while low faithfulness points to fixing the prompt.
svg.text: The RAG quality quartet: a 2×2 that localizes the failure
Four signals, split by which half of the pipeline they score
RETRIEVER
Did we fetch the right context?
Context precision
relevant retrieved ÷ total retrieved
Of the chunks we pulled, how many were
actually useful — or is there junk
alongside the good page?
low = noisy retrieval
Context recall
relevant retrieved ÷ total relevant
Of the chunks we needed, did we get
them all — or did we miss a page the
answer depended on?
0 = the answer is doomed before the LLM runs
GENERATOR
Did we use the context well?
Faithfulness
every claim supported by the context
Does the answer stick to the retrieved
pages, or does it invent facts the
context never stated?
low = hallucination
Answer relevance
does the answer address the question?
A grounded, faithful answer can still
be off-topic or evasive and never
actually answer what was asked.
low = evasive / off-topic
Whichever quadrant drops localizes the fix
context recall = 0 → fix retrieval • faithfulness low → fix the prompt • relevance low → the answer dodged the question
